```python
import re

def capital_words_spaces(s):
    return re.sub(r'(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])', ' ', s)
```

This inserts a space before every capital letter except one at the start of the string, so `"Python"` stays `"Python"` and `"PythonProgramming"` becomes `"Python Programming"`. The team note's "leading space" variant would return `" Python"` and fail the assert, so I didn't use it. The note's `(\w)([A-Z])` variant gives the same result on normal input, but on runs of capitals like `"ABC"` it gives `"A BC"` where this version gives `"A B C"`.
